scenes.sub: Proof-of-stake networks pay stakers to secure the chain. You either run a validator or delegate to one. Rewards come from issuance and fees. Risks: slashing (penalties for validator misbehaviour on some networks), unbonding periods (waiting time to withdraw) a
scenes.vo: Proof-of-stake networks pay stakers to secure the chain. You either run a validator or delegate to one. Rewards come from issuance and fees. Risks: slashing (penalties for validator misbehaviour on some networks), unbonding periods (waiting time to withdraw) and validator downtime.
scenes.cap: Proof-of-stake networks pay stakers to secure the chain. You either run a validator or delegate to one. Rewards come from issuance and fees. Risks: slashing (penalties for validator misbehaviour on some networks), unbonding periods (waiting time to withdraw) and validator downtime.

scenes.sub: Staking yields a few percent a year in the staked asset (e.g. ~3%, illustrative). Your dollar return is still dominated by the asset's price: +3% staking on an asset that falls 30% is still a large loss. Stake what you'd hold anyway.

lines: Does staking protect against price falls?
scenes.sub: Answer: No. It adds a small yield; price moves dominate.
